title: An integral algebra over a henselian pair gives a henselian pair
statement: Let $(A,I)$ be a henselian pair [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology] and let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings with $B$ integral over $A$ (every element of $B$ is a root of a monic polynomial with coefficients in the image of $A$). Then $(B,IB)$ is a henselian pair: for every finite $B$-algebra $C$, every idempotent of $C/IC$ lifts uniquely to an idempotent of $C$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma 15.11.8 (Tag 09XK, label lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2753), using the characterization (4) of Lemma 15.11.6 (Tag 09XI, lemma-characterize-henselian-pair: idempotent lifting for integral algebras)

proof.text: *$C$ is integral over $A$.* Let $C$ be a finite $B$-algebra, i.e. a ring map $B\to C$ of commutative rings making $C$ a finitely generated $B$-module. Then $C$ is integral over $B$ [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]. Since $B$ is integral over $A$, the composite $A\to B\to C$ makes $C$ integral over $A$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-transitive].

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 15.11.8 (Tag 09XK, lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2758: 'Immediate from the fourth characterization of henselian pairs in Lemma 09XI and the fact that the composition of integral ring maps is integral'); 'finite implies integral' is the observation in the proof of Lemma 09XI that (4) implies (3) trivially

proof.text: *$IC=(IB)C$.* Let $\varphi:A\to B$ and $\psi:B\to C$ be the structure maps. The ideal $IC$ of $C$ generated by $\psi(\varphi(I))$ and the ideal $(IB)C$ generated by $\psi(IB)$ coincide: $\psi(\varphi(I))\subseteq\psi(IB)$ gives $IC\subseteq(IB)C$; conversely an element of $IB$ is $\sum_k b_k\varphi(i_k)$ with $b_k\in B$, $i_k\in I$, so its image $\sum_k\psi(b_k)\psi(\varphi(i_k))$ lies in $IC$, whence $(IB)C\subseteq IC$. Hence $C/(IB)C=C/IC$ as quotients of $C$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma 15.11.8 (Tag 09XK, lemma-integral-over-henselian-pair, line 2758: 'Immediate from the fourth characterization of henselian pairs in Lemma 09XI and the fact that the composition of integral ring maps is integral'); the identification of the two ideals is implicit in the source and written out by the agent

proof.text: *Lifting.* By step 1, $C$ is an integral $A$-algebra via $A\to B\to C$, so, $(A,I)$ being henselian, the quotient map $C\to C/IC$ induces a bijection from the idempotents of $C$ to those of $C/IC$ [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-pair-integral-idempotent-lifting]. By step 2, $C/IC=C/(IB)C$, so every idempotent of $C/(IB)C$ lifts to an idempotent of $C$, and two idempotents of $C$ with the same image in $C/(IB)C$ are equal. As $C$ was an arbitrary finite $B$-algebra, $(B,IB)$ is a henselian pair by definition [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].
